new_entities.name: Clonazepam for REM sleep behavior disorder
aliases: clonazepam in REM sleep behavior disorder
new_entities.description: Use of bedtime clonazepam to reduce dream-enactment behaviors and episode burden in REM sleep behavior disorder.

new_entities.name: Episode frequency
new_entities.description: How often a recurrent symptom or disorder-specific episode occurs over time.

edges.effect_quant: Clonazepam remains a commonly used symptomatic therapy for REM sleep behavior disorder, but the direct evidence is weaker than its first-line reputation implies. A 2021 critical review found clear benefit reported in 684 of 1,026 clonazepam-treated patients across mostly uncontrolled clinical accounts, whereas the only placebo-controlled Parkinson disease RCT found no significant between-group difference after four weeks.
edges.population: adults with REM sleep behavior disorder, especially idiopathic or synucleinopathy-associated disease managed in outpatient sleep or neurology practice
edges.mechanism: Clonazepam likely suppresses motor expression of dream-enactment behaviors through benzodiazepine-mediated enhancement of inhibitory GABAergic signaling during sleep.
edges.summary: This is a cautiously protective edge rather than a cleanly settled one. Clonazepam is widely used and guideline-supported for symptom control, but the modern controlled trial signal is limited and not clearly positive.
edges.caveats: Most of the favorable literature consists of case series, retrospective cohorts, and mixed-etiology clinical reports rather than large randomized trials. Sedation, falls, cognitive adverse effects, and worsening of coexisting sleep apnea can limit usefulness in older adults.

evidence.notes: A critical review of the pharmacological treatment of REM sleep behavior disorder in adults: time for more and larger randomized placebo-controlled trials.

effect_quant.comparator: RBD patients reported as having clear benefit with clonazepam across aggregated clinical accounts in the review
